SECTION_V_HARD_STOP.conclusion: The TARGET_SHA source configures NO persistent DataProtection. The env key DataProtection__KeysPath the ticket assumed is a PHANTOM — the app never reads it, so setting it would be a forbidden guess. Production ALREADY runs ephemeral today (status quo since >= Aug 20), so this is not a regression introduced by the deploy.

IMPACT_ANALYSIS.auth_model: JWT Bearer (HMAC via Jwt__Key) — NOT DataProtection cookies. A restart does NOT log active users out; existing JWTs stay valid until expiry.
IMPACT_ANALYSIS.refresh_tokens: custom random strings stored in refresh_tokens table — NOT DataProtection-protected.
IMPACT_ANALYSIS.what_ephemeral_actually_affects: ASP.NET Identity default-token-provider artifacts only: outstanding password-reset links, email-confirmation links, and antiforgery tokens on open forms issued before a restart become invalid after it.
IMPACT_ANALYSIS.readiness_doc_correction: Prior readiness docs said restart may cause 'session invalidation'. Because auth is JWT, that is OVERSTATED — active sessions are NOT invalidated. Only the token artifacts above are.

OPTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.A_infra_home_persist_NO_CODE: Give www-data a stable writable HOME (systemd Environment=HOME=/var/lib/reporting) + create /var/lib/reporting/.aspnet/DataProtection-Keys (0700, www-data). The ASP.NET DEFAULT provider then persists keys there across restarts. Non-guessing, no code change, but relies on default-path discovery (not a config key) and keys unencrypted-at-rest (mitigated by 0700). DEVIATES from Section V literal wording (there is no config key) => needs owner OK.
OPTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.B_accept_ephemeral_documented: Keep status quo (ephemeral). Since auth is JWT, no active-session logout; only outstanding reset/confirm links + open-form antiforgery invalidate on the deploy restart. Prod already ephemeral today => no regression. Owner explicitly relaxes the Section V Hard Stop and accepts the documented limitation.
OPTIONS_FOR_OWNER_DECISION.C_abort_fix_in_source: Abort this deploy; add proper AddDataProtection().PersistKeysToFileSystem(...).SetApplicationName(...) reading a real config key to source, build a NEW candidate (new SHA != 7e063b4), re-test, re-authorize. Correct long-term fix but out of scope for TARGET_SHA and needs fresh authorization.

NEXT_REQUIRED_ACTION: Owner selects A, B, or C. No production write (backup/bridge/cutover) will occur until the owner resolves the Section V Hard Stop, per the ticket's own rule and 'stop on material deviation, do not bypass'.
